text: Objective: To analyze the association between depression and various health behaviors and to examine whether these associations differ by sex or income. Methods: This cross-sectional study used data from 65,803 Brazilian adults (aged 18–59 years) interviewed in the 2019 National Health Survey. Depression was assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9). The prevalence of smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, sedentary lifestyle, and dietary indicators was estimated according to the presence of depression. Analyses were stratified by sex and income, and prevalence ratios were estimated using Poisson regression. Results: A significant association was found between depression and all indicators studied, except occasional alcohol consumption. Depression was associated with heavy episodic drinking and insufficient consumption of fruits and vegetables only in women. In men, the associations of depression with sedentary lifestyle and with being a former smoker were stronger than in women. Occasional alcohol consumption was more prevalent only among men without depression. In the analysis stratified by income, the association between depression and physical inactivity was stronger in the higher-income group, whereas the association with heavy episodic drinking was significant only in the lower-income stratum. Conclusion: These results highlight the need to consider mental health in programs aimed at reducing harmful health behaviors, as well as the specificities of sociodemographic groups.

The handling and use of native species under laboratory conditions is the main obstacle to proposing species for use in bioassays. This study presents the results of rearing Paratanytarsus grimmii (Diptera: Chironomidae), a parthenogenetic species with a wide geographical distribution, under controlled conditions. Eggs were obtained from a pre-Andean river in the Araucanía region (39° S), and the conditions were determined for larval rearing with artificial food, adult handling, egg management (hatching synchronization), and collection of larvae after hatching. The life cycle of P. grimmii comprised a larval period of 23 days until the pupal stage (instars I to IV); within the following 48 hours, the adults laid eggs, which hatched after 72 hours. The following laboratory conditions were established: incubation room temperature, water pH, artificial feeding, photoperiod, and larval and egg management techniques. Because the entire life cycle could be maintained under laboratory conditions, this species can be proposed as a potential biological model for toxicity bioassays.

In Brazil, the illegal capture of wild animals is a crime that contributes to species extinction, in addition to causing environmental imbalance and animal suffering. Here, we conducted a quantitative survey of the animals sent to the Wild Animals Triage Centers (Centros de Triagem de Animais Silvestres, CETAS) in Porto Seguro, Salvador, and Vitória da Conquista during 2009–2019. A total of 19,317, 34,460, and 43,874 specimens were recorded in the units of Porto Seguro, Vitória da Conquista, and Salvador, respectively. By class, the totals comprised 80,948 birds (82.90%), 12,007 reptiles (12.30%), 4,661 mammals (4.77%), and 35 arachnids (0.03%). The most frequent operations generating records at the CETAS were apprehensions (67,974; 69.67%), followed by voluntary surrenders (13,367; 13.69%), rescues (12,803; 13.11%), and transfers (2,735; 2.67%). The animals came from 236 municipalities in the state of Bahia, mainly Salvador, Vitória da Conquista, Feira de Santana, Lençóis, Jequié, and Paulo Afonso. The quantitative assessment of seizures by municipality indicates that the BR-116 highway is one of the most important routes for the illegal trafficking of wild animals in the state of Bahia and in the country.

A prosocial lie is a false statement intended to help, rather than harm, someone. This study investigated the possible effects of age and culture on the responses of 97 Brazilian children (aged 7 to 11 years) in a prosocial lying task originally designed for a previous study with Canadian and Chinese children. The task consisted of four dilemmas, each followed by a question about what the child should do: tell the truth or lie to protect oneself, a friend, or a group. No effect of age was found on lying scores, but lying-for-friend scores were significantly higher than lying-for-self and lying-for-collective scores. This pattern of results suggests that, in contrast to Chinese and Canadian children, Brazilian children consider it more worthwhile to tell a lie that protects a friend than a lie that protects their own interests or those of a group.

For decades, teacher education has emphasized the importance of attending to the rapid and profound changes in society and in people's personal lives resulting from the widespread use of new digital technologies. Yet little has changed in schools, where traditional teaching still prevails. Students remain consumers rather than active producers of knowledge, and the use of technology for educational purposes continues to be seen as either a threat or an unattainable goal. However, the COVID-19 pandemic has compelled educational institutions to rethink the role of technology in education. In this article, we discuss the crisis that has struck higher education and how it has led our institutions, and ourselves as professors and teacher educators, into a deep process of rethinking our past practices and reimagining our future.

This study aimed to analyze the economic impact of adopting optimized, nutritionally balanced diets on Brazilian families, considering the Brazilian dietary guidelines and the economic disparities of the population. Data from the 2008–2009 Brazilian Household Budget Survey (550 strata; 55,970 households) were used. Approximately 1,700 foods and beverages purchased by Brazilians were classified into four groups according to the NOVA system. Linear programming models estimated isoenergetic diets, using the current diet as the baseline and gradually optimizing healthier diets based on the "golden rule" of the Brazilian dietary guidelines, while respecting nutritional constraints for macronutrients and micronutrients (based on international recommendations) and food acceptability limits (10th and 90th percentiles of the population's per capita calorie distribution). Diet cost was defined as the sum of the average cost of each food group in both the current and optimized diets (BRL per 2,000 kcal/person/day). The economic impact of the Brazilian dietary guidelines on household budgets was analyzed by comparing the cost of the optimized diets with that of the current diet, calculated for the total population and by income level. Three healthier diets were optimized. The current diet cost BRL 3.37 and differed between low- and high-income strata (BRL 2.62 and BRL 4.17, respectively). Regardless of income, diet cost decreased as diets approached the guidelines. However, low-income strata committed more than twice the share of their household budget committed by high-income strata (20.2% and 7.96%, respectively). Thus, the adoption of healthier eating practices can be achieved with the same or a lower budget.

This study aimed to identify the antioxidant responses of sugarcane (Saccharum spp.) varieties subjected to water and saline stress. Sugarcane seedlings of six varieties obtained through micropropagation were subjected to water stress, saline stress, or a combination of water and saline stress. The study was carried out in May 2012 in a greenhouse at the Universidade Federal Rural de Pernambuco (UFRPE). The experimental design was completely randomized, with treatments arranged in a 6 × 4 factorial scheme (six varieties and four treatments) with four replicates. Lipid peroxidation, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) concentration, and relative water content (RWC) were evaluated. In addition, the plants' antioxidative defense systems were assessed by measuring the activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), and catalase (CAT). The sugarcane varieties showed higher lipid peroxidation and/or higher H2O2 concentrations under combined water and saline stress. The antioxidant enzymes responded differently to the water and saline stress treatments depending on the variety. Under combined water and saline stress, however, the enzymes may have become inactivated, indicating that the response to combined stress differed from the sum of the responses to water stress alone or saline stress alone. High malondialdehyde (MDA) concentrations associated with low RWC may be an effective indicator of sensitivity to multiple stresses in sugarcane varieties. The varieties RB99395 and RB867515 responded more efficiently to environmental stress and maintained their cell water content under either water or saline stress.

Given the need to understand the variables related to the choice of Psychology specialties, this study aimed to present the adaptation process and verify validity evidence based on the internal structure of the Portuguese version of the Scale of Interests by Areas of Psychology (EIAPsi), and to relate it to personality. The sample consisted of 340 Portuguese university students who completed the EIAPsi and the NEO Five-Factor Inventory (NEO-FFI). Exploratory factor analysis and correlations between the instruments were performed. A factorial structure of 10 factors was found for the EIAPsi, with satisfactory reliability indices. The dimensions of openness and agreeableness were the most frequently correlated with the areas of Psychology. We conclude that initial validity evidence for the instrument was obtained, indicating its potential use in the Portuguese context, specifically in situations aimed at self-knowledge (in the classroom or clinic/office) and at guiding students in choosing their area of expertise.

This study aimed to evaluate the vertical transmission of Neospora caninum in naturally infected sheep and to monitor the kinetics of antibodies against this protozoan in their lambs. Forty-eight pregnant ewes from five herds were divided into two groups: G1, seropositive for anti-N. caninum antibodies (n = 19); and G2, seronegative (n = 29). Blood samples were collected from the ewes and their lambs immediately after birth, before colostrum intake, and at 2, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, and 56 days after birth. Serum antibodies were analyzed using the indirect immunofluorescence antibody test. Among the 19 seropositive ewes, six (31.6%) gave birth to lambs that were seropositive before ingesting colostrum, and these lambs remained positive until the end of the study (56 days). Only one lamb, born to a ewe with an antibody titer of 200, seroconverted after colostrum ingestion. All lambs born to seronegative ewes remained negative throughout the experimental period. We conclude that transplacental transmission was an important route of N. caninum dissemination in the herds studied and that seropositive lambs maintained circulating antibodies during the period analyzed.

This pilot case study had two aims: to explore power and voice in small-group interactions in a secondary school classroom, and to examine the implications of researching one's own practice as a teacher-researcher. Drawing on Bakhtin's theory of dialogism, audio recordings of one small-group interaction were compared with students' independent written work to understand whose voices were used and how. Four main themes were identified: power and authority, positions of submission, silence, and the voice of the text. The findings also showed that, in the midst of teaching, we can fail to see these power and identity dynamics, whereas the time and space afforded by reflective research enable researchers to see beyond the moment and to view their teaching interventions and strategies anew, supporting the construction of new meaning.

In this article, residual indicators were used to characterize the quality of the numerical solution of the advection-diffusion-reaction equation in a saturated porous medium. Both large and small advection regimes were considered. Small advection was exemplified by a problem with constant data, whereas non-constant data were considered for the large advection regime. In the latter case, residual quantities associated with the data must be incorporated into the residual estimates related to the spatial approximation, and an auxiliary problem must be solved to correctly obtain the temporal estimates. Presenting the residual indicators as a surface over the finite element mesh provides a detailed view of the regions that require refinement, allows the effect of each estimate on the composition of the global estimator to be inferred, and makes it possible to follow the evolution of the residual surfaces as the contaminant front advances during the simulation. In turn, the numerical values of the indicators make it possible to delimit the elements to be refined, to compare the magnitudes of the contributions with one another and across different meshes, and to better understand the composition of the global estimates.

We present a checklist of Odonata (Insecta) species occurring in a fragment of Seasonal Deciduous Forest (Atlantic Forest biome) in the central region of the state of Rio Grande do Sul (RS), southern Brazil, together with a list of the odonate species recorded in this phytoecological region of the state. In addition, we comment on the seasonal distribution of the species occurring in the study area. Two streams and seven farm ponds located in the middle course of the Jacuí River basin were surveyed between December 2007 and February 2009. Overall, we recorded 49 species from 21 genera and six families. Argia serva Hagen in Selys, 1865 (Coenagrionidae) was recorded for the first time in the state, raising to 183 the total number of Odonata species known to occur in Rio Grande do Sul. The number of species recorded in the study area corresponds to ~26% of the known Odonata diversity in RS. Libellulidae was the most species-rich family (22 species, ~45% of the total), followed by Coenagrionidae (18 species, 37% of the total). The checklist for the Seasonal Deciduous Forest in RS indicated the occurrence of 83 Odonata species in this phytoecological region (~45% of the known odonate species in the state). This high diversity may be related to the density of the vegetation structure. In the study area, 20 species were found in streams and 45 in farm ponds. Species occurrence showed marked seasonal patterns, with 88% of the species recorded from summer to autumn and no species detected in streams in winter. Moreover, 70% of the species were recorded in only one or two seasons in farm ponds, while 65% occurred in only one season in streams. These results indicate that the life cycle of Odonata in southern Brazil is strongly influenced by seasonal patterns in temperature.

Introduction: Peripheral vestibular disorders can lead to cognitive deficits and are more common in elderly patients. Objective: To evaluate and correlate cognitive, balance, and gait aspects in elderly women with chronic peripheral vestibular dizziness, and to compare them with elderly women without vestibular disorders. Methods: Twenty-two women with episodes of peripheral vestibular dizziness for at least six months participated in the study. They were categorized by dizziness severity as moderate (n = 11) or severe (n = 11). The control group (n = 11) comprised women with no vestibulopathy, light-headedness, or dizziness. Cognitive assessments and semi-static and dynamic balance assessments were performed with the Balance Master (Neurocom International, Inc., Clackamas, OR), while the Dizziness Handicap Inventory provided a score for symptom severity. Inferential statistics and correlation analyses were applied to the cognitive, balance, and stability variables across the groups. Results: The group with severe dizziness showed higher sway velocity of the center of pressure in the anteroposterior direction, shorter step length, and slower gait than the control group. Regarding the cognitive variables, the group with severe dizziness symptoms showed significant correlations with stability and gait variables. Conclusion: The relationship between cognitive aspects, balance, and gait was stronger in women with severe dizziness than in those without vestibulopathy.

This study aims to identify the different practices found in innovation environments belonging to National Innovation Systems with distinct maturity levels: France (advanced) and Brazil (in development). A case study compared the Technological Park of São José dos Campos and the Pôle de Compétitivité HYDREOS across seven dimensions: governance, strategy, external relationships, external environment, legal context, infrastructure, and funding mechanisms. The results support the initial premise that the environment embedded in the mature system presents a more comprehensive set of the studied dimensions. The main differences identified, which also represent improvement opportunities for the Brazilian environment, concern external relationships, strategy, funding mechanisms, and governance. Most of these differences directly affect the degree of interaction among the members of the innovation environment and between them and external actors, the diversity of actors, and the relationship rules, which are key elements of a national innovation system.

Research in education indicates that the Philosophy for Children (P4C) curriculum is instrumental in achieving important educational objectives. Yet it is precisely this instrumentalist conception of P4C that has been challenged by a second generation of P4C scholars. Among other things, these scholars argue that P4C must remain vigilant toward, and avoid subscribing to, (1) developmentalism and (2) a reductive identification of thinking with rationality. On the contrary, they suggest that P4C must give voice to childhood, allowing it to enter into genuine dialogue with adulthood. Scholars who defend a non-reductive and non-instrumentalist approach to P4C highlight the significance of play in philosophy sessions with children. In this paper, I examine the extent to which the philosophical inquiry that takes place in the context of P4C can be understood as a playful activity. I submit that Fink's account of play can help us better understand what we mean by play, which in turn can help us examine the compatibility between the activities of P4C and play. In the first part of the paper, I examine some of the basic ideas of P4C and raise the question of the compatibility of philosophical inquiry and play. In the second part, I engage in a philosophical appreciation of play by drawing on the work of Eugen Fink. In the final part, I show how play, understood along Fink's lines, is compatible with philosophical inquiry as practiced in school settings.

Experimental measurements of systems with slow gas transport kinetics are generally considered easier than measurements of very fast systems. However, when the transport process has time constants of the order of several hours, not only the measurements but also the analysis and interpretation of the data become challenging, making the determination of the correct time constant non-trivial. In this work, we used measurements of CO2 diffusion in Na,Cs-Rho crystals, carried out using the zero length column (ZLC) technique, as a case study for the application of the technique to very slow adsorption processes. The system, which has a time constant of the order of 8 h, demonstrates the importance of the partial loading approach for unambiguously determining the time constant from the analysis of ZLC desorption curves. The traditional analysis is refined by using the nonlinear ZLC model to account for the isotherm nonlinearity that results in a concentration-dependent diffusivity. Finally, the method proposed by Cavalcante is used to confirm the three-dimensional diffusion path of the system.

General aspects of the chemistry of dithiocarbamates, their metal complexes, and their interactions with important enzymes: a brief review. Dithiocarbamates (DTCs) comprise a series of compounds belonging to the class of 1,1-dithiolates. The use of these organic molecules in the coordination chemistry of several metals has been well explored in recent decades, along with their potential applications in medicinal chemistry. Given our expertise in this field, including the synthesis of new DTCs, their coordination chemistry with various metal cations, and their biocidal activities, we summarize in this manuscript the outcomes of selected investigations reported in the literature on the interactions of DTCs or their complexes with key enzymes such as carbonic anhydrases, superoxide dismutase, urease, tyrosinase, glutathione-related enzymes, caspases, and dehydrogenases. We first provide a brief introduction to the chemistry of DTCs, covering their electrochemistry, kinetics of formation, solubility, and stability toward solvation. The following sections summarize the results of experiments on the inhibition of these enzymes by DTCs and some of their coordination complexes. Final remarks and conclusions are presented at the end of the manuscript.

Language attrition has become a vibrant research topic because of its implications for theoretical linguistics, including the organization of linguistic information in the brain and language processing. Insights from this area also affect the study of second language (L2) development and can inform language teaching. Because language attrition may be valuable for the study of language retention and maintenance, it can contribute to language teaching with long-lasting results, more effective planning, and better syllabus design. In this context, as studies exploring L2 attrition are still limited, this article provides a synthesis of research in the area. Drawing on the Dynamic Model of Multilingualism and the Threshold Hypothesis, it also explores the implications of L2 attrition research for language teaching, with a view to establishing more informed language practices and policies.

Data from field experiments conducted in Festival table grape vineyards in Petrolina, PE, Brazil, from October 2009 to November 2010, were used to evaluate the influence of plastic cover on the productivity and economic profitability of viticulture in the São Francisco River Valley. Three treatments were studied: uncovered canopy (UC), plastic cover placed 50 cm above the canopy (PC50), and plastic cover placed 100 cm above the canopy (PC100). The results indicated that the greater availability of radiative fluxes at berry height in PC100 contributed to higher productivity, whereas PC50 had the lowest availability of radiative fluxes at berry height and a much lower productivity. The yield obtained in PC100 exceeded those of UC and PC50 by 11 t ha-1 and 12.3 t ha-1, respectively. PC100 also had the lowest amount of berry defects, which contributed to higher total revenue. By contrast, PC50 had markedly lower productivity, which represented considerable economic losses.

Ethnic Tibetan farm and herder households (FHH) in Gansu Province, China, are stricken by poverty. Solving the poverty problem in this and other poverty pockets across China is of particular importance for the country's political stability, ethnic unity, social well-being, and ecological security. This paper assesses the multidimensional poverty of ethnic Tibetan FHH in Gansu Province, China, using the Alkire-Foster method. Twelve indicators are included in the multidimensional poverty indicator system. The results showed that (1) in the single-indicator measure, adult family members having at least a 9th-grade education (x3), home toilet type (x7), and labor availability (x2) showed a higher incidence of deprivation; (2) many FHH in the Tibetan areas of Gansu Province face multidimensional poverty, but the proportion of extreme poverty is very small; and (3) in terms of contribution rate, adult family members having at least a 9th-grade education (x3), labor availability (x2), self-health assessment (x1), home toilet type (x7), and school-age children dropout rate (x4) occupied the top five positions under the equal weight to dimensions (DEW) method.

This study aimed to assess the level of disclosure of the survival, growth, and profitability (SGP) construct in the mission statements of Brazilian companies and in the collective discourse of different economic sectors, classified according to the "Biggest & Best" yearbook published by Exame Magazine. It addresses a gap in the literature by examining the disclosure of the SGP construct in the mission statements of large Brazilian companies. Because the mission statement is the genesis of strategic planning, analyzing the disclosure of the SGP construct allows us to discuss how relevant the mission statement is to the elaboration, implementation, and monitoring of that planning. The benefit of a mission statement aligned with strategic planning lies in communicating long-term SGP goals adequately to stakeholders, on the assumption that comprehensive and objective communication minimizes the risk of failures during the management process. Collective subject discourse (CSD) was used to develop a metric for qualifying the constitutive elements of organizational mission statements, making it possible to identify whether Brazilian companies, grouped into different economic sectors, smooth, conceal, or omit the construct formed by the SGP components in their mission statements. We investigated the presence or absence of the SGP components in the collective discourse of the mission statements of 220 large Brazilian companies. Most of the companies in the sample do not include SGP in their mission statements, and those that do address it with discursive vagueness, lacking clarity in the disclosure of its components. For academia, this finding contributes to understanding the constituent components of the mission statements of large Brazilian companies. For organizations, the findings indicate the need to reflect on the content used to formulate their mission statements.

Cover crop straw may alter microbial activity and populations, with repercussions for environmental change and for C and N dynamics, thereby providing important information for planning appropriate land use in the Cerrado. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of cover crop straw on soil microbial attributes and organic matter quality. Experimental units consisted of 100 g of sieved soil placed in small plastic cups and mixed with straw from cover plants. Treatments were distributed in a completely randomized design (CRD) with a 7 × 7 + 1 factorial scheme, comprising seven types of straw evaluated at 7, 14, 21, 28, 42, 63, and 105 days after incubation, plus a control without straw, with three replicates. The metabolic quotient (qCO2) ranged from 0.1 (Crotalaria spectabilis at 14 days) to 5.1% (Cajanus cajan 'IAPAR 43' at 42 days). The organic carbon and nitrogen reservoirs were affected differently by legume and grass straw across the evaluation dates. The incorporation of Brachiaria brizantha and Mucuna aterrima had a positive impact on the microbial attributes (qCO2, Cmic, and Nmic) up to the 21st day of incubation, with little loss of carbon dioxide and growth of the microbial population. All the species evaluated showed potential for use in crop rotation systems, enabling no-tillage systems in the Cerrado of Piauí. However, species should be selected according to specific purposes. Thus, the use of cover crops is an important tool for improving the biological quality of soils in the Brazilian northeastern Cerrado.

Aim: To report the occurrence of Apistogrammoides pucallpaensis in Brazilian territory, as its known distribution has so far been restricted to Peru and Colombia. Methods: Specimens were collected in 2013 during an ichthyofauna survey of the Auati-Paraná region, located in the Mamirauá Reserve, state of Amazonas. Nets were used in the floating aquatic vegetation, and rapichés (hand nets) were used in the coastal region. Apistogrammoides is the only genus among the Geophaginae with 6–9 spines in the anal fin, whereas Apistogramma has 3–4. Results: The specimens showed three evident marks on the caudal fin and a black stripe on the side of the body running from the eye to the caudal peduncle; these features distinguish the genus. Conclusions: This study extends the known distribution of A. pucallpaensis and constitutes the first record of the species for Brazil.

Given the growing volume of research on Thysanoptera in Brazil, studies have been conducted to improve our understanding of thrips diversity in areas where the fauna has historically been neglected. Accordingly, we recorded the diversity of thrips (Insecta: Thysanoptera) associated with a restinga fragment on the campus of the State University of Ceará (UECE), Fortaleza, Ceará state, and calculated estimated richness and diversity indices. Samples were collected from 2011 to 2013 from the flowers of 86 plant species. The material was taken to the Laboratory of Insect-Plant Interaction, where thrips were screened under a stereomicroscope. We collected 456 adults and 58 immatures, representing 14 species, in addition to one unidentified species of Treherniella. Microcephalothrips abdominalis was found on a large number of host plants, and Frankliniella insularis was the most common species. About two-thirds of the total thrips species richness was associated with three plant families (Amaranthaceae, Caesalpiniaceae, and Poaceae), and six thrips species were each associated with only one plant species. The observed species richness was close to that estimated by the Bootstrap and Jackknife 1 estimators. The Shannon-Wiener (H') and Simpson (D) diversity indices were 1.7607 and 0.7769, respectively. Although the species are common, 46 new associations between plant species and thrips were established, 13 of which are true host associations, demonstrating the importance of coastal vegetation in maintaining thrips populations.

In this paper, we elaborate on the consequences of a post-humanist perspective for the problem of physical disability by approaching the use of assistive technologies (ATs) by disabled people as the introduction of a low-tech cyborg into the world. In doing so, we highlight examples of communication ATs and draw analogies between ATs and languages in the constitution of selves and social contexts. ATs are ideologically informed; they can be seen either as a way to "fix" an "impaired" person or as a strategy to overcome a physical and social context that disables some people and makes others "able-bodied." We argue that becoming a low-tech cyborg can be a form of social inclusion if disability is understood as produced by the context rather than as an inherent dysfunctionality of the individual. Based on this assumption, we identify two strategies of social inclusion for the low-tech cyborg: disembodiment of the Self and embodied virtuality. We note, however, that low-tech cyborgs can be configured out of necessity or by choice, and that the same socioeconomic factors that produce inequality in general also operate in the social exclusion or inclusion of the low-tech cyborg. Thus, ATs can be adopted and transformed by choice in ways that widen the gap between cyborg haves and have-nots, while both kinds of cyborgs may become increasingly subject to cognitive and affective exploitation in the context of cognitive capitalism. We conclude that the potential of a post-humanist perspective on disability lies not in making "impaired humans" whole, nor in making "whole humans" more than human, but in keeping selves ethically connected with others, whether through virtual embodiment or embodied virtuality.

The design of water distribution systems involves, above all, determining the pipe size that meets the system's requirements while minimizing annual installation and operation costs. Among the existing methodologies for determining the economic pipe diameter, Bresse's equation remains common among designers. This work analyzes the efficiency of Bresse's equation, the MBPW, and the MLVPC by comparing them with the MREC. We recommend that designers not use the MBPW or the MLVPC. For small water distribution systems, Bresse's equation can be used, provided that an appropriate value is adopted for its coefficient k. For HDPE, we propose k = 1.17 or k = 1.18. For PVC DEFOFO and GFRP, we suggest ranges of 1.19 to 1.23 and 1.29 to 1.32, respectively. For larger water distribution systems, we recommend the MREC as the methodology for determining the economic pipe diameter, because an appropriate value for Bresse's coefficient cannot be established.

Aim: To evaluate the general state of research on the decomposition of organic matter in aquatic environments in the subtropical region of South America. Methods: We compiled publications (1990–2018) using a combination of terms referring to decomposition, detritus, aquatic environments, and South American countries with subtropical climates. The characteristics of the publications were analyzed over time. Results: A total of 1,042 publications were found, of which 106 specifically addressed the purpose of this study. For subtropical South America, this research topic is incipient. Most studies were carried out in streams (39.6%) and addressed the decomposition process and associated invertebrates (42.5%). Studies in lentic environments (e.g., lakes, 10%) are markedly scarce. Conclusions: Studies on the decomposition of organic detritus in aquatic ecosystems in the subtropical region of South America are still emerging. While the role of shredders is moderately well understood, the importance of microorganisms in the decomposition process still needs to be better evaluated. Finally, our study showed that scientific collaboration boosted publication on the topic.

This paper introduces PeMSyn, a free tool intended to aid the design and simulation of permanent magnet synchronous machines. Using PeMSyn, one can easily design a permanent magnet synchronous machine, define its winding distribution, and assess its performance. Machine performance is evaluated by finite element analysis (FEA), as PeMSyn provides an interface between Matlab and FEMM, allowing several machine parameters to be obtained. Another notable characteristic of PeMSyn is its modularity: each functionality can be run independently, and new functionalities and machine topologies can be added either by the user or through a PeMSyn update. To be simple and user-friendly, PeMSyn was coded in Matlab as a graphical user interface (GUI). Moreover, users can easily translate all labels and variable names into their native language using a language description file, already available in English and Portuguese. The modules, the machine design process, the equations involved, and an application are presented in this paper. To provide guidelines on how to use PeMSyn, an example of machine design is proposed and its performance is assessed.

The main objective of this research was to evaluate the reading time of street names on dynamic egocentrically referenced maps for In-Car Route Guidance and Navigation Systems. Two road network patterns (grid-like and non-grid-like) were considered, and tasks were devised to search for street names in two route segments (where the driver was and where the driver would have to maneuver). In the non-grid-like road network pattern, for the task of searching for the name of a road where the driver would maneuver, street names aligned horizontally and next to the route were read significantly faster than street names positioned along the route. Street names positioned obliquely required more reading time than street names aligned horizontally. Dynamic egocentrically referenced maps should present street names horizontally aligned and next to the route for the segment where the driver will maneuver, for both road network patterns. In addition, street names should be positioned next to the car symbol.

The Annonaceae is one of the most anatomically and structurally uniform plant families. Chemotaxonomy is a common practice for determining chemical patterns within such families at different phylogenetic levels. The aim of this study was to build a dataset of all secondary metabolites isolated from the Annonaceae family and to perform the respective chemotaxonomic analysis using self-organizing maps (SOMs). The dataset comprises 5321 botanical occurrences and 1860 unique molecules present in all subfamilies of the Annonaceae. Diterpenes account for 366 unique compounds and 533 botanical occurrences, found in both the Annonoideae and Malmeoideae subfamilies. The tribes Annoneae, Xylopieae, and Miliuseae had the highest numbers of botanical occurrences and were therefore selected for analysis. Molecular descriptors of the diterpenes and their respective botanical occurrences were used to generate the SOMs. These SOMs showed clear and indicative separation of the tribes, with a match rate higher than 70%. Our results corroborate the morphological and molecular data. These models can be used to predict the phylogenetic location of certain diterpenes and to accelerate research on Annonaceae secondary metabolites and their biological potential.

This article situates South Tyrol among other multinational states, such as Flanders, Québec and Catalonia, in an attempt to broaden models of multilevel governance, especially with regard to the accommodation of migrants. It also examines how language policies affect migrants settled in this Italian multinational context, drawing on data from semi-structured interviews that capture migrants' perspectives on the policy of declaration of linguistic affiliation or aggregation and on its effects on social division. Participants also raised the topics of racism and xenophobia in connection with linguistic issues involving the non-legitimation of the speaker. The findings show that migrants perceive the declaration policy as a burden: some of the participants stated that they do not feel represented by it, and that it reinforces social division.

This study discusses the possibilities of adopting digital resources for teaching and learning English as a second language (L2) in higher education in general and at a public university in Brazil in particular. Key aspects of the literature review, which covers approaches such as Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL), Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) and English-Medium Instruction (EMI), are compared with the context and activities of a university in the Global South in order to discuss the use of digital resources in L2 English teaching and learning. The results suggest that a critical use of technologies is necessary to promote a more balanced and sustainable language teaching and learning process. Institutional support is also essential for teachers and students to develop the skills required in an increasingly interconnected world. We conclude that a combination of alternative practices, supported by digital resources, can foster effective language teaching and learning in higher education institutions.

Background: Procedures that reduce errors during repertoire learning play an important role in Applied Behavior Analysis for people with autism, given the detrimental effects that excessive exposure to error may have on learning. Previous studies have investigated the effects of correction procedures that require an active student response after an error trial. Some intervention manuals recommend against reinforcing responses after correction to prevent the establishment of prompt dependence. This study directly investigated the effect of reinforcement after an active-response correction procedure during tact training in four children with autism. An echoic-to-tact training procedure was used to teach tacts. A "no reinforcement after correction" (NRC) condition was compared with a "reinforcement after correction" (RC) condition using an adapted alternating treatments design. Results: All participants required fewer correction trials in the RC condition than in the NRC condition. Across all 26 sessions in which both training procedures were implemented, participants' performance was higher with RC than with NRC in 17 sessions and was the same in 3 sessions. Conclusions: We discuss the effectiveness of reinforcing correct responding after an active-response correction procedure, the absence of prompt dependence, and the implications of better correction procedures for applied settings.

The Brazilian semiarid region is historically characterized by a scarcity of good-quality water. Although groundwater reserves are abundant in this region, these waters have high concentrations of dissolved salts, which makes them unsuitable for irrigating most crops. The objective of this study was to evaluate the growth, production and salinity tolerance of three cauliflower cultivars grown in NFT (Nutrient Film Technique) hydroponics and subjected to different electrical conductivities of the nutrient solution (ECsol) prepared with saline water. The experiment was carried out in a randomized block design with a split-plot arrangement and six replications. Plants were subjected to six ECsol levels (1.94 [control], 3.24, 4.10, 5.04, 5.92 and 7.01 dS m⁻¹) in the main plots, and three cauliflower cultivars ('Piracicaba de Verão', 'Sabrina' and 'SF1758'), grown in the same hydroponic channel, were allocated to the subplots. Vegetative growth, inflorescence production and cultivar salinity tolerance were evaluated. In general, except for the number of leaves, leaf width, and leaf and shoot fresh matter, the ECsol levels negatively affected the vegetative growth and inflorescence yield of the cauliflower cultivars. The cultivars 'Piracicaba de Verão' and 'Sabrina' were considered moderately sensitive to salinity, whereas 'SF1758' was considered moderately tolerant.

Objective: To investigate the use of health services and limitations in performing usual activities among adults and older adults with and without noncommunicable chronic diseases (NCDs), according to sociodemographic strata. Methods: This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the 2019 National Health Survey. The final sample comprised 88,531 households in which interviews were completed, referring to individuals aged 18 years and older. The prevalence of service use in the population with NCDs was compared with that in the population without NCDs and stratified by socioeconomic and demographic variables. Prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were calculated. Results: In 2019, 47.6% (95%CI 47.0–48.3) of the population reported having one or more NCDs. Compared with the population without NCDs, those with NCDs had more medical consultations in the previous 12 months (adjusted PR [APR]=1.21; 95%CI 1.20–1.23), used more health services in the previous 2 weeks (APR=2.01; 95%CI 1.91–2.11), had more hospitalizations (APR=2.11; 95%CI 1.89–2.36), and had more limitations in performing usual activities (APR=2.52; 95%CI 2.30–2.76). A positive dose–response gradient was observed between the number of comorbidities and the use of services. In all socioeconomic and demographic strata, the prevalence of the indicators was higher in people with NCDs. Conclusion: The presence of NCDs was associated with greater use of health services (i.e., consultations, service use, and hospitalization) and with greater restriction of usual activities in all socioeconomic and demographic strata.

Brazilian Bill n. 6,299/2002, which addresses pesticide regulation, represents an attempt to loosen and weaken the regulation of these substances, threatening the rights to food and to a healthy environment enshrined in the Constitution of the Federative Republic of Brazil. This article reviews the bill and its most problematic provisions through the lenses of food and nutrition security and of the principles and provisions of national environmental law. Against this background, the paper concludes that Bill n. 6,299/2002 undermines previously achieved progress in providing alternative policy pathways for sustainable agriculture in Brazil. It conflicts with environmental law principles, neglecting precaution and prevention and representing a regression in protection levels, while undermining the human rights to food and to a healthy environment. The methodology comprises a literature and documentary review combined with inductive reasoning.

Paulo Nenflidio describes himself, in his biographical note, as an artist who works at the intersection of art, science and technology. A multifaceted and inventive artist, he produces sculptures, installations, objects, instruments and drawings in which sound, electronics, movement, construction, invention, randomness, physics, control, automatons and workarounds come together as elements of artistic expression. He holds a degree in Fine Arts from the School of Communication and Arts of the University of São Paulo and is a graduate electronics technician of the Lauro Gomes Technical School in São Bernardo do Campo. Born in São Bernardo do Campo, he maintains his studio in this city. In this interview, we seek to deepen our study of the poetics of Nenflidio's work. The conversation addresses how his creative trajectory developed, the conceptual inspirations that guided his creative processes and artistic research, and the role of sound and silence as forms of poetic expression. The interview was conducted by email between 20 and 24 July 2021.

Embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS) is an important subgroup of cryptogenic strokes that has recently received attention owing to ongoing trials. We reviewed the medical records, at discharge from the stroke unit, of all patients who met ESUS criteria and were treated at our institution between February 2016 and July 2017. Among 550 stroke patients, 51 had ESUS. Hypertension (60%), diabetes mellitus (34%) and smoking (36%) were the most prevalent risk factors. The mean National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores were 7 at admission and 4 at discharge, while the median modified Rankin Scale scores were 0 at admission and 2 at discharge. Our sample showed ages, risk factor prevalence and NIHSS scores at admission and discharge similar to those of European and North American cohorts. Although our cohort was small, our findings suggest that the ESUS population is similar across countries with different health financing systems.

This article aims to identify the changes in corporate governance associated with the life cycle of companies. It is guided by the research problem of understanding the effects of business maturity on ownership structure, corporate relations and other governance configurations. The study used a longitudinal analysis of the changes that occurred at Transportadora Brasileira Gasoduto Bolívia-Brasil SA (TBG), a privately held company controlled by Petrobras Logística de Gás, with the participation of several state and private partners. Data were collected through document analysis and interviews with executives. The results identified a relationship between the stages of the business and the characteristics of its investors, ranging from an initial phase built around energy companies specialized in the business to a maturity phase in which the investment became attractive to capitalist partners interested in financial returns. In addition, planning before capital consolidation, the existence of a financing structure, clear criteria for selecting partners, and the presence of a second relevant shareholder mitigate problems of abuse of power or non-compliance with established rules, helping to preserve the relationship between shareholders over time and the sustainability of corporate agreements. The study contributes a new perspective on the analysis of corporate governance, considering the changes and adaptations required over time and offering reflections on corporate structures and the priorities of governance actors.

In his contribution to the Special Issue "Digital and semiotic mechanisms of contemporary populisms," Jan Blommaert offers a communicability model that accounts for political discourse (and other discourses) in the post-digital era. He begins by arguing that the idea of the public as a homogeneous entity, which was very popular in the twentieth-century sociological imagination of how propaganda worked in "manufacturing consent," can no longer explain the fragmented audiences of the post-digital era. He illustrates his argument with the circulation of political tweets and retweets as texts in an algorithm-oriented world, a circulation that targets niche audiences. In the final section, he argues that discourse analysts need to operate from this communicability model if they are to understand the crucial role of political discourse in contemporary social life.

This study assessed heavy metal concentrations in sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) and spinach associated with uncontrolled municipal waste, motor vehicle fumes, pesticides, and fertilizer in the urban west region of Zanzibar. Twenty samples were randomly collected from local markets and from three farms located along a roadside in the urban west region. The samples were analysed using energy dispersive X-ray fluorescence at the Tanzania Atomic Energy Commission in Arusha. Essential and toxic elements (Mn, Cu, Fe, As, Zn, Pb, and Ni) were detected in both sweet potato and spinach. Sweet potato had higher concentrations of Cr, Fe, Cd, and Zn, whereas spinach had higher concentrations of Ni, Cr, and Zn. The concentrations of essential elements in the vegetables analysed were within the safety baseline levels for human consumption. However, the concentrations of toxic elements exceeded the FAO/WHO permissible limits. The higher concentrations of toxic elements in sweet potato and spinach might be associated with contamination from municipal waste, chicken manure, motor vehicle fumes, or pesticides. Therefore, vegetable cultivation along roadsides in the urban west region of Zanzibar, together with the use of fertilizer and chicken manure, may introduce high levels of heavy metals into the food chain.

This study investigated the genetic diversity of the 'Zuijinxiang' grape and its F1 mutant breeding plants in order to screen excellent mutants with potential breeding value. Fifty mutated single plants obtained from 137Cs-γ-irradiated 'Zuijinxiang' grape seeds were used as research material. SCoT molecular markers were used for genetic diversity and variation analysis, and cluster analysis was performed. The results were as follows. (1) Thirty-six SCoT primers produced abundant polymorphisms with clearly visible bands; the amplification efficiency and polymorphism rate were 100%. (2) A total of 221 bands were amplified by the 36 primers, of which 175 were polymorphic; the average percentage of polymorphism was 80.3%, and the average genetic similarity coefficient was 0.916. (3) The number of observed alleles (Na) ranged from 4 to 8, with an average of 6.1389; the number of effective alleles (Ne) ranged from 1.2772 to 5.6322, with an average of 3.5968; the expected heterozygosity (He) ranged from 0.2192 to 0.8344, with an average of 0.6965; the observed heterozygosity (Ho) ranged from 0.1656 to 0.7808, with an average of 0.3035; Nei's gene diversity index (H) ranged from 0.2170 to 0.8224, with an average of 0.6863; and the Shannon-Wiener index (I) ranged from 0.5186 to 1.8597, with an average of 1.4517. (4) UPGMA clustering of the 51 materials showed that they could be divided into three groups at a genetic distance of 0.856. These results indicate that the irradiation-induced variant germplasm of 'Zuijinxiang' is genetically rich. In addition, SCoT markers can distinguish materials with close genetic distances and can be used for the early identification of grape mutant materials. This study provides a theoretical basis for developing excellent mutant germplasm of 'Zuijinxiang' grape.

Silicon and proline play important physiological, metabolic, and functional roles in plants, especially under water deficit. Their application can mitigate the adverse effects of stress in crops by increasing water use efficiency and antioxidant activity. This study aimed to evaluate silicon (Si) as an attenuator of the effects of water deficit on cowpea cultivars, using physiological, biochemical, and growth indicators. The experiment followed a randomized block design with four cultivars (BRS Guariba, BRS Itaim, BRS Aracê, and BRS Rouxinol) and four irrigation treatments, with or without Si application (W100, 100% ETo; W50, 50% ETo; W50+100Si and W50+200Si, with 100 and 200 mg L-1 of silicon, respectively), in a 4 × 4 factorial scheme with five replicates. Leaf water potential, proline concentration, antioxidant enzymes, and growth indicators were evaluated in the cowpea plants. Under water deficit, all cultivars showed reduced leaf water potential, which compromised plant growth. However, Si applications of 200 mg L-1 in BRS Guariba and of 100 and 200 mg L-1 in BRS Itaim minimized the effects of stress by increasing leaf water potential and ascorbate peroxidase activity in both cultivars. Proline concentration increased in the former and decreased in the latter, and growth was maintained in both. Although they did not increase water potential, Si applications of 100 and 200 mg L-1 in BRS Rouxinol and BRS Aracê, respectively, reduced the deleterious effects of stress on growth by regulating enzymatic metabolism and proline.

The electrochemical reduction of nitrofurazone (NF) was studied by cyclic voltammetry (CV) and square wave voltammetry (SWV) in a non-aqueous medium, using three different ionic liquids (ILs), BMImTf2N, BMImBF4, and BMMImTf2N, with a carbon fiber microelectrode as the working electrode. In all of them, two reversible cathodic peaks were recorded for NF. At higher frequencies, only one reversible cathodic peak was observed. The reversibility of the systems was also evident by CV, since a reversible redox couple was recorded for this reduction. The reversibility of the systems, with adsorption of product and reagent on the electrode surface, was confirmed, and the number of electrons involved in the reduction indicated the formation of the nitro anion radical followed by its respective dianion. For the first reduction, an EC mechanism (an electrochemical step followed by a chemical step) was proposed for the systems in aprotic medium, in which a probable second-order chemical reaction follows the charge transfer process. The kinetic constants were calculated using the Olmstead and Nicholson model.

Subsistence fishing is a confusing and heterogeneous fishery construct. Even so, its connection to human protection compels us to analyze it through the lens of human rights. Using Chile as a case study because of its legal peculiarities, we aim to determine the scope of Chilean legislation on subsistence fishing, integrating international human rights treaties, case law, and reports from United Nations agencies, with regard to three issues. First, we examine how Chilean legislation relates to the right to food and the promotion of decent social conditions. Second, we explain why the prohibition of riggings and propulsion enables the identification of economically precarious users, and how this prohibition relates to vulnerability and poverty as human rights concepts. Finally, we show how the property rights of indigenous peoples and the culture of fisherfolk populations could require their inclusion and preferential treatment in access to subsistence fishing resources. Considering these results, we argue that human rights help to clarify the understanding of subsistence fishing, and we propose partial amendments to the Chilean legislation. Above all, however, human rights introduce protection standards that allow us to see such legislation not as a mere derivation of state privilege, but as an attempt to foster equality: an affirmative action. We conclude by presenting a conceptual approach to Chilean subsistence fishing, suggesting that it could help to unveil new objectives and rights in fishing and even influence the understanding of natural resource allocation.

The bearing capacity of saturated soils can be estimated using effective or total stress approaches, which extend the concepts proposed by Terzaghi (1943) and Skempton (1948), respectively. Recent studies have shown that similar approaches (i.e., the Modified Effective Stress Approach, MESA, and the Modified Total Stress Approach, MTSA) can be used to interpret and predict the bearing capacity of unsaturated soils by considering the influence of matric suction. However, a comprehensive discussion of the application of MESA and MTSA in geotechnical engineering practice is lacking in the literature. In this state-of-the-art paper, the background associated with MESA and MTSA is therefore introduced first. The analytical and numerical methods available in the literature for predicting the bearing capacity of unsaturated soils are then revisited. The available methods are explained by categorizing them into two groups, MESA and MTSA, and their applications are illustrated with examples. This state-of-the-art paper aims not only to provide tools for a rational understanding of the bearing capacity of unsaturated soils but also to improve its prediction, so that these approaches can be extended to geotechnical engineering practice.

Despite their small share of the economy, agricultural activities are of significant importance in the Porto Alegre metropolitan region (PAMR), Rio Grande do Sul State, Brazil. This has been reflected in efforts to consolidate these activities, especially in the family farm model. To evaluate soil characteristics and to understand the perceptions and assessments of producers, two settlements in the PAMR were visited, and housing and production areas of family farms were selected for this study. Tools such as semi-structured interviews and guided walks were used, and some plots were selected for soil sampling and observation. The results showed that the soils of the settlements have limitations for agricultural use, such as low natural chemical fertility, sandy texture, and drainage restrictions. Local producers can distinguish these characteristics, and comparisons with the land of their places of origin were important for this. Local people more readily understood field approaches, which highlights the need for such tools to foster dialogue among technicians, researchers, and the target population. It was possible to recognize correspondences between local people's observations and the technical-scientific attributes used in land suitability evaluations, showing a rapprochement between these types of knowledge and allowing the participatory planning of sustainable production systems.

Mothers' and fathers' conceptualizations of joy, sadness, anger, fear, pride, and shame were assessed, as were their beliefs regarding the importance of children's expression of these emotions and their connection with the profiles of autonomy, relatedness, and autonomous-relatedness. Sixty mother-father dyads with children up to three years old participated in the study. Questionnaires on parents' conceptualizations of emotions were used. Most participants considered joy an important emotion for children of their kids' age to express (with an individual motivational character). However, anger, pride, and shame were associated with older children. Mothers' and fathers' conceptualizations and beliefs did not diverge. The autonomous-related self model correlated positively with the importance that mothers and fathers attributed to all the emotions studied.

For manufactured homes, the Light Gauge Steel Frame system lacks an in-depth study of the relationship between its assembly techniques and the behavior of assembly-line-based production systems. This article therefore presents the development of a flow shop production system using assembly lines for the production of Light Gauge Steel Frame modular houses. The main result was that the system was able to deliver a house in slightly more than eight working hours, using four-hour cycles. An experimental research procedure with computational simulation was used. The abstracted model of the designed system was simulated, and its behavior was analyzed with respect to improvement hypotheses proposed in four different scenarios. The results are relevant because they fill gaps in the body of knowledge by using Light Gauge Steel Frame as a technology for producing manufactured houses on assembly lines, and they also provide performance and design parameters for implementing the proposed solution in the real estate market.

Thermotherapy of sugarcane setts is currently the primary management method for Leifsonia xyli subsp. xyli (Lxx) in Brazil. When the setts are immersed, the enzymes and proteins of the bacterial cell are denatured without harming the sett buds. Because the bacterium may escape detection and survive thermotherapy, possibly resulting in asymptomatic seedlings, this study aimed to detect Leifsonia xyli subsp. xyli in sugarcane setts using molecular techniques and different time and temperature combinations, with or without the addition of antibiotics. Conventional PCR detected Lxx DNA only in the positive control, which consisted of a highly susceptible plant with a high bacterial concentration. Using nested PCR, Lxx DNA was detected in all treatments. Thus, none of the thermotherapy treatments eliminated Lxx from the setts, and the use of kasugamycin also did not eliminate the bacterium, although it reduced the bacterial population in the tested treatments. These results confirm that nested PCR is a useful tool for detecting this phytobacterium in setts to be used as seedlings.

In this paper, we first analyze the atmosphere as a gas mixture per unit mass governed by the Van der Waals equation, considering the main components of air and their respective critical properties (critical temperature, TC, and critical pressure, pC). After adjusting the corresponding constants, which we denote I and D, we obtain the Van der Waals equation of state for the atmosphere in this context. Next, we analyze the order of magnitude of the terms in this equation and propose a Van der Waals-like equation of state that depends only on D, which we call the WD equation of state. In addition, we consider a physical approach to the Van der Waals equation for the atmosphere, studying the pressure terms associated with intermolecular repulsive and attractive forces in air, and we again obtain the WD equation of state. With this new proposal, we verify that the potential temperature and the equivalent potential temperature retain the same expressions as those established in atmospheric thermodynamics under the ideal gas law. However, we find corrections that depend on D in both the alternative form of the first law of thermodynamics and the virtual temperature.

Objective: To analyze the association between the occurrence of new tuberculosis cases and the Adapted Living Conditions Index, and to describe the spatial distribution of the disease in an endemic municipality. Method: This analytical ecological study was based on new cases among residents of an endemic municipality in the North Region of Brazil. Data were obtained from the Notifiable Diseases Information System and the 2010 Demographic Census. The Adapted Living Conditions Index was derived by factor analysis, and its association with the occurrence of the disease was assessed using the chi-square test, with the type I error set at 0.05. Kernel estimation was used to describe the density of tuberculosis in each census sector. Results: The incidence coefficient was 97.5 per 100,000 inhabitants. There was a statistically significant association between the number of cases and socioeconomic class, with membership in the highest economic class reducing the chance of disease occurrence. Thematic maps showed that tuberculosis was heterogeneously distributed, with a concentration in the southern region of the municipality. Conclusion: The association of tuberculosis with precarious living conditions reinforces the importance of discussing social determinants in the health-disease process, in order to support equitable health actions in risk areas in contexts of vulnerability.

Bottom-dwelling elasmobranchs, such as guitarfishes, skates and stingrays, are highly susceptible to bycatch because their distributions overlap with areas of fishing operations. Catch data for this group are also often merged into generic categories, which prevents species-specific assessments. Along the east coast of Australia, the Eastern Fiddler Ray, Trygonorrhina fasciata (Müller & Henle, 1841), and the Sydney Skate, Dentiraja australis (Macleay, 1884), are common components of bycatch, yet little information is available on their age, growth and reproductive timing, which makes impact assessment difficult. In this study, we estimate and report age and growth (from vertebral bands) as well as reproductive parameters for these two species, based on 171 Eastern Fiddler Rays (100 females and 71 males) and 81 Sydney Skates (47 females and 34 males). Based on von Bertalanffy growth curve fits, Eastern Fiddler Rays grew to larger sizes than Sydney Skates but did so more slowly (ray: L∞ = 109.61, t0 = 0.26 and K = 0.20; skate: L∞ = 51.95, t0 = −0.99 and K = 0.34; sexes combined). Both species had higher liver weight ratios (HSI) during the austral summer. Gonadal weight ratios (GSI) were higher in the austral winter for Eastern Fiddler Rays and in the austral spring for Sydney Skates.

The debate on climate change has begun to influence public policy through technical documents that include predictions and impacts concerning the environment, society, the economy and culture. In this context, research and intellectual contributions on the theme have focused on developing mechanisms to avoid or mitigate the approaching global crisis. In this review, taking a somewhat different perspective, we present the work of Frank Fischer, who, accepting the inevitability of the crisis, adopts a line of political debate on "the place of democracy" in a context of established global disaster. We highlight his main arguments, including the authoritarian tendencies that emerge as a means of confronting the crisis, as well as the structures and mechanisms for defending democracy, and we bring into the discussion perspectives on eco-localism and its associated elements. We also analyze the potential and some of the weaknesses of Fischer's arguments. Fischer is an author who has become established as a fundamental reference for those engaged with the subject.

Development in glycosylation methods: a key to access applications in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Glycosylation is an important class of reactions in organic chemistry, and the development of new methods contributes to the synthesis of many biologically active compounds containing various glycosidic bonds. It is arguably the most important, albeit challenging, reaction in carbohydrate chemistry. Examples of glycosylation products include glycoproteins, glycolipids, glycosaminoglycans, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. Glycosylation types are classified according to the identity of the atom that links the carbohydrate chain, namely C-linked, N-linked, O-linked or S-linked. In this short review, we describe recent reports on the main glycosylation methods, their basic mechanisms, the factors influencing stereoselectivity, and their applications in the synthesis of bioactive molecules.

Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a disease characterized by progressive loss of muscle fibers, advancing gradually from proximal to distal muscles. Although a few studies have investigated hand grip strength in non-ambulatory patients with DMD, the literature on its relationship with functional capacity is lacking. Objective: To determine the associations between hand grip strength and functional measures in non-ambulatory children with DMD. Methods: Hand grip strength was evaluated using a dynamometer in children with DMD. The children were also assessed with the Turkish version of the Egen Klassifikation Scale Version 2 (EK2) for global functional capacity, the Performance of Upper Limb (PUL) for upper limb functional performance, and the ABILHAND-Kids for hand ability. Results: The mean age of the 38 children with DMD was 12.02 ± 1.99 years. Dominant hand grip strength was higher than non-dominant hand grip strength (p < 0.05). The EK2, PUL and ABILHAND-Kids scores were 13.02 ± 5.50, 49.86 ± 14.34 and 26.81 ± 7.59, respectively. Hand grip strength was correlated with the EK2 score (p < 0.05). Conclusions: Measuring functional ability and strength in very weak children with DMD is known to be difficult and complex for therapists and clinicians in the clinical setting. Although the correlation is moderate, hand grip strength may be used in clinical practice as a practical assessment tool to gain immediate insight into global functional capacity in non-ambulatory children with DMD.

Introduction: The integrity of articular cartilage determines the functional state of the joint. In recent years, the development of MRI sequences for the assessment of various articular cartilages has become the focus of many research topics. Objective: To retrospectively study the diagnostic accuracy of three-dimensional MRI sequences for knee cartilage injury caused by sports-related trauma. Methods: Forty-six knee joints of 45 patients with sports injuries underwent multi-sequence MRI before surgery, including conventional knee MRI (SE T1WI, FSE PD/T2WI), 3D SPGR and 3D FIESTA sequences. Results: According to the surgical findings, 3D SPGR combined with conventional MRI sequences achieved the highest sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value in the evaluation of cartilage damage: 73%, 98%, 95% and 90%, respectively. Conclusions: 3D SPGR combined with conventional MRI sequences can improve the accuracy of evaluation and diagnosis of cartilage disease within a reasonable scan time. Level of evidence II; Therapeutic studies – investigation of treatment results.

Bartonella is a genus of emerging zoonotic bacteria mainly associated with mammalian erythrocytes and endothelial cells. Bats are natural reservoirs of a variety of important pathogens that affect human and animal health. Recent reports have highlighted the role of bats and bat flies in the maintenance of Bartonella. Here, we show that none of the 29 bat blood DNA samples obtained from five bat species on São Luís Island, state of Maranhão, northeastern Brazil, was positive for Bartonella in qPCR assays targeting nuoG. In contrast, three of 15 DNA samples (20%) from flies of the family Streblidae were positive for Bartonella. BLASTn results showed that the gltA and rpoB sequences shared identities ranging from 97.2% to 100% with Bartonella sequences amplified from bats or bat flies from Costa Rica and Brazil. These findings were supported by phylogenetic analyses based on Bayesian inference. The present study shows that Bartonella genotypes are present in bat flies, thus shedding light on the distribution of bat fly-related Bartonella genotypes in South America.

The current study analyzes Chilean students' and parents' perceptions of English language assessment. A total of 352 Chilean 10th graders were surveyed using the Perceptions of the Assessment Tasks Inventory, the Perceived Classroom Assessment Environment Scale and the Test Anxiety Scale to measure their perceptions of English language assessment. A semi-structured interview was also conducted to capture the perceptions of 74 parents regarding English and the way their children are assessed in the English subject. The quantitative data were analyzed using the Pearson correlation coefficient to measure the strength of the relationships among scores on the three scales, and the qualitative data were categorized using content and frequency analysis. The findings suggest that the subscales of the three surveys are significantly related and that students feel a learning-oriented assessment environment benefits them more than a performance-oriented one. The former favors students' learning and mastery of subject materials, whereas the latter aligns with classroom assessment practices that emphasize grades over learning. The qualitative results also suggest that parents have a positive perception of the English language and believe it is useful for their children's lives, even though they may themselves find it difficult to learn.

Context: While the digital economy requires a new generation of technology for scientists and practitioners, the software engineering (SE) field faces a gender crisis. SE research is a global enterprise that requires the participation of both genders for the advancement of science and evidence-based practice. However, women across the world tend to be significantly underrepresented in such research, frequently receiving less funding than men and appearing less often as authors of research publications. Data on this phenomenon remain sparse and incomplete; in particular, in evidence-based software engineering (EBSE), no studies have analyzed the participation of women. Objective: To present the results of a systematic mapping study (SM) conducted to collect and evaluate evidence on female researchers who have contributed to the area of EBSE. Method: We performed the SM by manually searching the major EBSE conferences and journals. We identified 981 studies, of which 183 were authored or co-authored by women and were therefore included. Results: Contributions from women to secondary studies have increased globally over the years but remain concentrated in European countries. Additionally, collaboration among research groups is still fragile and relies on a few women acting as bridges. Latin American researchers contribute substantially to the field, although they do not collaborate extensively within their own region. Conclusions: The findings of this study are expected to add to existing knowledge about women's contributions to the EBSE area. We hope that our results prompt reflection on the gender issue and motivate actions and policies to attract female researchers to this area.

Nuclear techniques based on the attenuation of gamma radiation are used in industry to measure flow rate, determine fluid density, predict inorganic scale in oil pipelines, and evaluate industrial mixers, among other applications. Applying these techniques requires studying key parameters of the radioactive source and radiation detectors that form part of the measurement geometry, such as detection efficiency and solid angle. The aim of this study was to calculate the solid angle and the effective solid angle subtended by a NaI(Tl) detector. The effective solid angle accounts for attenuation in the medium between the source and the detector, as well as other effects of radiation interaction with matter. Mathematical models were developed using the MCNP6 code to evaluate the proposed measurement geometry. The source was placed at different positions relative to the detector to evaluate the frontal and lateral solid angle contributions, an important parameter for obtaining the intrinsic efficiency response function. The simulated model consisted of a NaI(Tl) scintillator detector and two isotropic point sources (241Am and 137Cs). For the geometry used in this study, the difference between the solid angle and the effective solid angle reached 20.17% for 241Am and 2.58% for 137Cs, indicating that the effective solid angle should be considered in these calculations.

This paper analyzes the role of industrial policy in promoting technological upgrading in Brazil. To this end, we focus on the main characteristics of the Brazilian national innovation system and the role of its institutions. We examine whether the industrial policy implemented between 2003 and 2014 was able to change agents' conventions towards more vigorous strategies linked to technological upgrading and catch-up. In addition, we analyze the Brazilian mining industry, a sector in which Brazil has developed relevant competitive advantages in international markets and in which domestic agents have built important operational capabilities. Our main results, based on the unsuccessful policy experiences between 2002 and 2014, show the considerable difficulties faced by industrial policy in establishing mechanisms to drive technological catch-up. The specific experience of the Brazilian mining industry confirms these general findings, since domestic mining companies were unable to create new technological capabilities, even during the commodity price boom.

This article analyzes temporality in Leon Kirchner's Interlude I for solo piano in light of Jonathan Kramer's book The Time of Music. The first section introduces the composer, covering his biography, influences, and compositional style. The second section presents Kramer's book and his concepts of linear and nonlinear time in music. An analysis of aspects of the Interlude's linear time, as defined by Kramer, follows, including linearity manifested through developing variation, stepwise motion, tonal references, tempo changes, flexion count changes, and transpositions. The next section examines manifestations of nonlinear time in the Interlude, such as balance and recapitulation, and discusses the implications of Kramer's concept of nonlinear moment time. The conclusion summarizes the interactions between linearity and nonlinearity in the Interlude.

This work aims to verify the influence of the characteristic compressive cylinder strength (fck), section geometry, and eccentric axial load on the strength of square, cross-shaped, T-shaped, and L-shaped reinforced concrete sections under oblique composite flexion. A computational algorithm was developed to calculate the bending strength interaction diagrams of the sections, considering the idealized parabola-rectangle stress-strain relationships of NBR 6118 for concretes with fck from 20 to 90 MPa. The results show that the influence of fck is stronger at higher axial loads and that the shape of the failure surface in the interaction diagrams depends directly on fck and on the distribution of rebars in the section. Furthermore, under lower compressive axial loads, higher oblique composite flexion strengths are achieved when more reinforcement area is located in tension regions; as compression increases, however, the presence of reinforcement and larger concrete areas in compression zones provide higher bending moment strengths.

Purpose: This study presents a guide to using grounded theory methods for exploring organizational phenomena in the new online era. Design/methodology/approach: A reflexive account is adopted of how one can build upon the foundations of traditional offline grounded theory to conduct grounded theorizing with online-based data. Findings: Guidelines are presented for conducting grounded theory in online contexts, including crafting research questions, gathering online data, and using consolidated methods for analyzing online data.
